issues.legal_issue: Secondary evidence cannot be received to prove the contents of an instrument that is chargeable with stamp duty but remains insufficiently stamped.
material_facts: The parties relied on a written agreement to grant a lease that was insufficiently stamped.
The original agreement was not produced; the party seeking to rely on it offered oral evidence of its execution and contents.
The original was alleged to have remained with the opposing parties, who suppressed it.
The objection to the oral evidence was raised at the final-argument stage, after the evidence had been recorded.
issues.conclusion: The oral evidence was inadmissible. The statutory bar on acting upon an insufficiently stamped instrument also bars secondary evidence of its contents; the exception for an instrument admitted without objection does not extend to secondary evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 35 and 36 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, read with the definition of instrument in section 2(14), govern admissibility notwithstanding that sections 59–65 and 91 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, may permit secondary evidence in the circumstances. Section 35 bars both admission of the instrument and acting upon it unless it is duly stamped. Its proviso (a) permits admission upon payment of the duty or deficiency and penalty only when the original instrument is before the court. A copy or oral account of the contents is not itself the instrument. Section 36 applies only where the original instrument was admitted without objection at the initial stage and does not validate secondary evidence. The court relied on Raja of Bobbili v. Inuganti China Sitaramaswami Garu, State of Bihar v. Karam Chand Thapar & Bros. Ltd., Thaji Beebi v. Tirumalappa Pillai, and Chidambaram v. Meyyappan; it disapproved Maung Po Htoo v. Ma Ma Gyi and the relevant dictum in Satyavati v. Pallayya, and explained Ponnuswami v. Kailasam and Alimana Sahiba v. Subbarayudu.

predicates.secondary_evidence_admissibility_proceed: The proceeding concerns whether evidence other than the original may be received to prove the contents of a document.
predicates.secondary_evidence_sought: A party offers a copy or oral account to prove the contents of a document rather than producing the original instrument.
predicates.original_instrument_stamp_defect_uncured: The original instrument is chargeable with stamp duty and its stamp deficiency has not been cured by producing it and paying the required duty or deficiency and penalty.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns secondary evidence, a party seeks to prove a document's contents without the original, and the original's stamp deficiency remains uncured, the secondary evidence is barred.

issues.legal_issue: A post-judgment application to add future mesne profits to a decree is not granted where the claimant had stated in its own pleading that it would seek those profits in a separate suit and the courts below did not award them.
material_facts: The respondents applied in the Supreme Court to add relief for future mesne profits to the decree.
In their own plaint, the respondents had stated that they would bring a separate suit to recover future mesne profits.
The courts below had not granted that relief.
issues.conclusion: The application to add future mesne profits to the decree was refused on the facts of the case.
issues.legal_principle: The court identified the application as one under Order 47 Rule 3 of the Supreme Court Rules and refused it on the facts: the applicants had pleaded that they would pursue future mesne profits in a separate suit, and the courts below had accordingly granted no such relief. The court cited no earlier cases or broader substantive rule for this refusal.

rule.if: post_judgment_decree_amendment_application and future_mesne_profits_sought and separate_suit_announced_in_pleading and lower_courts_omitted_relief

predicates.post_judgment_decree_amendment_applicati: A party applies after judgment to add relief to an existing decree.
predicates.future_mesne_profits_sought: The party asks for future mesne profits to be included in the decree.
predicates.separate_suit_announced_in_pleading: The party had stated in its own pleading that it would seek future mesne profits in a separate suit.
predicates.lower_courts_omitted_relief: The courts below did not include future mesne profits in the relief granted.

issues.definition: When a party makes a post-judgment application seeking future mesne profits, had announced in its pleading that it would seek them in a separate suit, and the courts below omitted that relief, the profits are not added to the decree.
